messages.author: Archana
messages.body: Sir, what is the meaning and how to remove, Function 'rism1d_closure_get 3drismbackground' at (1) has no Implicit type; of error message while running tutorial-T0.

messages.body:

>Sir, what is the meaning and how to remove, Function 'rism1d_closure_get
>3drismbackground' at (1) has no Implicit type; of error message while
>running tutorial-T0.
We need a more explicit description of the problem.  What, exactly, do you
mean by "tutorial-T0"?  What part of the tutorial were you running?  The
message looks like it comes from a compilation step (but I could be wrong

...thanks...dac

messages.author: Archana
messages.body:
Sorry sir,
My query was that, after getting 'amber installation complete' message, I have started to run the tutorials provided on the amber home page for practice purpose. When giving xleap command it show's the message 'xleap command not found'. To remove this, first I have tried to install xleap in my ubantu but at the last step I found the error message  'Function 'rism1d_closure_get 3drismbackground' at (1) has no Implicit type;'. Now I am not understanding the error. Please sir help me to removing this type of error.

messages.author: Dr. Anselm Horn
messages.body:
Archana,
maybe your Amber installation was without any X11 support, so xleap was
not compiled and installed. As a workaround, you could simply use the
non-graphical tleap for your purpose.
Regards,
Anselm

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Nov 16, 2021, Archana wrote:
>When giving xleap command it show's the message 'xleap
>command not found'.
Is there an xleap file in your $AMBERHOME/bin folder?  Have you sourced
the "amber.sh" file in $AMBERHOME?  Do other programs (e.g. tleap) work?
>To remove this, first I have tried to install xleap in my ubantu.....
Can you say exactly what you did to "try to install xleap"?  What was
different this time than when you originally installed the codes?
You are falling into the (common) trap of reporting what your intentions
were, and not saying *exactly* what you typed, and what the response was.
You should also report what OS and compiler version you are using.
...thanks...dac
